title: Battle of Crécy
summary: On 26 August 1346 in northern France, an English army under Edward III defeated a larger French army under Philip VI during the Hundred Years' War. Longbowmen and dismounted men-at-arms broke repeated French charges, causing heavy French losses. The English then besieged Calais, which fell the following year, and the battle established the longbow's effectiveness.

as_recorded.value: The Battle of Crécy took place on 26 August 1346 in northern France

importance.justification: Major Hundred Years' War battle that showed the longbow's power over cavalry and led to the fall of Calais.

audience_note: Describes battlefield mass death, including thousands of casualties.
